raw_text:
Thanks — I’ve built a 12‑week, gym‑based program you can start 2026‑06‑01 for your 31‑year‑old female client with PCOS (irregular cycles, some anovulatory), HbA1c 5.8, BMI 28. The plan prioritizes resistance training to improve insulin sensitivity and body composition, avoids excessive cardio and aggressive calorie restriction (to protect HPA axis), and includes recovery, nutrition guidance, and monitoring cues.

Structure overview
- Frequency: 4 resistance sessions/week (2 lower, 2 upper; full‑body emphasis across week), plus 1 optional low‑impact conditioning or active recovery session. Two full rest days/week.
- Progression: 3 phases (Foundation 1: weeks 1–4, Strength & muscle build 2: weeks 5–8, Intensification & metabolic finish 3: weeks 9–12). Load, volume and intensity ramp progressively.
- Session length: ~45–65 minutes.
- Cardio: brief, low‑to‑moderate intensity intervals or steady low‑impact work ≤2x/wk and kept short (15–25 minutes) to avoid overtraining and under‑fueling.
- Nutrition: moderate calorie deficit or body‑recomposition approach (no crash diets), prioritize protein, protein timing, distribution of carbs around training, adequate fats to support hormones, and adequate total energy. Guidance below includes macros and practical rules.
- Recovery & monitoring: sleep, stress, RPE, menstrual/energy tracking; adjust if signs of under‑recovery (persistent fatigue, sleep loss, mood change, >10% performance drop).
- Medical note: follow endocrinologist guidance, monitor glucose/HbA1c progress, report any new symptoms.

Weekly layout (typical)
- Monday: Upper A (Push emphasis) — strength + accessory
- Tuesday: Lower A (Posterior emphasis + heavies)
- Wednesday: Rest or light mobility/recovery walk / yoga
- Thursday: Upper B (Pull emphasis) — strength + accessory
- Friday: Lower B (Quad emphasis + metabolic finisher)
- Saturday: Optional low‑impact conditioning (15–25 min) or active recovery
- Sunday: Rest

Progression principles
- Weeks 1–4: build technique, movement quality, metabolic conditioning, moderate volume. RPE mostly 6–8.
- Weeks 5–8: increase load (heavier compound lifts), moderate hypertrophy volume. RPE 7–9 on main sets.
- Weeks 9–12: higher intensity and purposeful metabolic density rounds to optimize insulin sensitivity and body composition, but avoid excessive volume. Include occasional cluster/contrast sets and short metabolic finishers. RPE 8–9 on main sets; deload approach built into final week if needed based on fatigue.

Detailed week‑by‑week plan
Phase 1 — Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: movement quality, baseline strength, metabolic conditioning, establish consistent nutrition and recovery habits.

Progression: Use a 2×/week progression scheme—aim to increase weight when you can complete top range with good form.

Week 1 (start 2026‑06‑01)
Monday — Upper A (Push focus)
- Warm‑up: 5–8 min row + dynamic shoulder/torso mobility
- Barbell bench press (or dumbbell) 4 × 6–8, RPE 7
- Seated DB shoulder press 3 × 8–10
- Incline DB chest fly or cable 3 × 10–12
- Triceps rope pushdown 3 × 12–15
- Core: Pallof press 3 × 30s each side
- Cool down: mobility, 5 min stretching

Tuesday — Lower A (Posterior bias)
- Warm‑up: 6–8 min bike + hip mobility
- Romanian deadlift (RDL) 4 × 6–8, RPE 7
- Goblet squat 3 × 10–12
- Glute bridge or hip thrust 3 × 8–10
- Single‑leg Romanian deadlift (light) 2 × 10 each
- Calf raises 3 × 12–15
- Finish: 8–10 min easy walk or bike (zone 1–2) for recovery

Thursday — Upper B (Pull focus)
- Warm‑up: 5–8 min row + scapular prep
- Bent‑over row or chest‑supported row 4 × 6–8
- Lat pulldown or assisted pull‑up 3 × 8–10
- Face pulls 3 × 12–15
- Biceps curls (DB or bar) 3 × 10–12
- Core: Dead bug 3 × 10 each side

Friday — Lower B (Quadriceps bias + conditioning)
- Warm‑up: 6–8 min bike + ankle mobility
- Back squat or safety bar squat 4 × 6–8
- Bulgarian split squat 3 × 8–10 each leg
- Leg press (moderate) 3 × 10–12
- Hamstring curl 3 × 12–15
- Metabolic finisher: 10 min AMRAP (easy) — 10 kettlebell swings, 10 bodyweight squats, 10 calorie row (keep RPE 6–7)
- Cool down/mobility

Saturday — Optional: 15–20 min brisk walk, yoga or mobility

Weeks 2–4
- Keep same structure. Increase loads when you can complete top number of reps with good form. Aim 0.5–2.5 kg increases on main lifts when able.
- Week 4: make week slightly heavier on main lifts but reduce accessory volume by ~10–15% in week 4 if fatigue appears (mini deload).

Phase 2 — Strength & Hypertrophy (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: increase strength on big compounds, hypertrophy to support metabolic improvements, maintain recovery.

General changes
- Main compounds become heavier (4–6 rep range for 2 of 4 main compound work sets), accessory sets 8–12.
- Add one PAUSED or tempo set weekly to stimulate control.
- Slightly shorter conditioning but maintain 1 optional session.

Weeks 5–8 schedule (representative Week 6)
Monday — Upper A
- Bench press 5 × 5 (build to heavy set, RPE 8)
- DB incline press 3 × 8
- Overhead press 3 × 6–8
- Cable chest fly 3 × 12
- Triceps dips (assisted if needed) 3 × 8–10
- Core plank variations 3 × 40–60s

Tuesday — Lower A
- Deadlift or trap bar deadlift 4 × 4–6 (build intensity, RPE 8)
- Barbell hip thrust 4 × 6–8
- Walking lunges 3 × 10 each leg
- Swiss ball hamstring curl 3 × 12
- Calf raises 4 × 12–15

Thursday — Upper B
- Weighted pull‑ups or lat pulldown 4 × 6–8
- Barbell row or one‑arm row 4 × 6–8
- Seated cable row (tempo 3s ecc) 3 × 8–10
- Rear delt fly 3 × 12–15
- Biceps superset (curl variations) 3 × 10–12

Friday — Lower B (Quad focus + metabolic)
- Front squat or pause low‑bar back squat 4 × 5–6
- Leg press 3 × 8–10
- Romanian single‑leg deadlift 3 × 8 each
- Glute medius band work 3 × 15 each side
- Short metabolic finisher: 12–15 min EMOM or 3 rounds: 250m row + 12 kettlebell swings + 12 walking lunges (keep moderate intensity, avoid all‑out)

Saturday — Optional 20 min low‑impact cardio (cycle or elliptical) zone 2

Notes for phase 2
- Emphasize progressive overload but avoid pushing to failure each set—leave 1–2 reps in reserve on accessory work.
- Check-in after week 6 for energy, sleep, mood. If persistent fatigue, reduce volume by 10–20% for one week.

Phase 3 — Intensification & Metabolic Finish (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: consolidate strength and increase metabolic responses for improved insulin sensitivity without excessive volume.

General changes
- Alternate heavier and moderate weeks (wave loading). Include one higher‑density session per week and one heavier compound day.
- Finishers target interval work or circuits of resistance movements rather than long steady cardio.
- Week 12 include an active recovery/deload depending on fatigue (trainer judgement).

Representative Week 10
Monday — Upper A (heavy)
- Bench press 5 × 3 (work up to heavy sets, RPE 8–9)
- Weighted pull‑up 4 × 5 (or heavy lat pulldown)
- Incline DB press 3 × 8
- Face pulls 3 × 15
- Triceps heavy finish 3 × 6–8

Tuesday — Lower A (density)
- Complex/metabolic density: 4 rounds, 60s each exercise, 90s rest between rounds:
  - Trap bar deadlift (6 reps)
  - Kettlebell swing (12)
  - Reverse lunge (8 each)
  - Plank 45s
- Finish: single heavy set back squat 3 × 5 (moderate weight)

Thursday — Upper B (volume + speed)
- Push‑pull superset circuit: 4 rounds
  - Plyo or speed push (med DB bench speed) × 6
  - Chest‑supported row × 8
  - Overhead press × 8
  - Band pull‑aparts × 15
- Biceps/triceps superset 3 × 10

Friday — Lower B (strength + metabolic)
- Barbell squat 4 × 4–6 (heavy)
- Romanian deadlift 3 × 6–8
- Bulgarian split squat 3 × 8 each
- Short finisher: 8–12 min AMRAP moderate — 12 calorie ski/row, 10 goblet squats, 12 KB swings

Saturday — Optional: 15–20 min low‑impact zone 2 or mobility class

Week 12 (final week) — Deload/assessment
- Reduce volume 40–50% and intensity 10–20% depending on fatigue. Focus on technique, mobility, and re-testing a few metrics (e.g., 3‑rep back squat, 3‑rep bench) if client feels recovered.
- Reassess body metrics, HbA1c follow up scheduling with endocrinologist as appropriate.

Exercise choices and substitutions
- Use machine or DB alternatives if joint pain or technique issues.
- For clients who can’t do heavy deadlifts/squats, use trap bar or safety bar as safer heavy alternatives.
- Emphasize posterior chain (hip thrusts, RDLs) to improve insulin sensitivity via large muscle mass stimulation.

Nutrition guidance (to protect hormones and improve insulin sensitivity)
- Objective: modest energy deficit or body‑recomp if client prefers to maintain weight and recomposition. Aim for -200 to -300 kcal/day below maintenance (or maintenance if losing weight quickly or signs of under‑fueling).
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight/day (for a 28 BMI female, roughly target 90–120 g/day depending on weight). Distribute across 3–4 meals with 20–40 g per meal prioritized around training.
- Carbohydrate: moderate, prioritized around training windows — 30–50% of calories; more carbs on training days, less on rest days. Focus on low‑GI carbs and whole foods.
- Fat: 25–35% of calories, avoid very low‑fat intakes; include sources of omega‑3s and monounsaturated fats to support hormones.
- Meal timing: include a carb‑containing meal or snack 1–3 hours pre‑training and protein + carb within 1–2 hours post‑training to support recovery and insulin sensitivity.
- Avoid crash diets, intermittent extreme fasting, or excessive cardio which can worsen HPA axis and menstrual function.
- Micronutrients: ensure adequate iron (monitor ferritin/Hb given HbA1c close to prediabetic range), vitamin D, magnesium. If low energy or irregular cycles persist, review with MD and consider targeted labs (TSH, free T4/T3, ferritin, vitamin D).
- Hydration: aim for consistent hydration, 2–3 L/day depending on sweat losses.

Recovery, monitoring & signs to adjust program
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours/night.
- Track: RPE per session, resting HR, mood, sleep quality, menstrual tracking or ovulation signs if possible. With PCOS irregularity, track energy and any changes in symptoms.
- Reduce training volume or intensity if:
  - Persistent >7 days of fatigue, sleep disturbance, irritability.
  - Performance declines >10% across multiple workouts.
  - Weight loss progresses >0.5–1% bodyweight/week and energy falls.
- Increase calories by 150–300 kcal/day and reduce conditioning if signs of under‑fuelling appear.

Insulin sensitivity specific notes
- Resistance training (particularly heavy compound lifts and large‑muscle movements) increases GLUT4 translocation and improves insulin sensitivity — program emphasizes these.
- High intensity conditioning is included sparingly and kept short (<15–20 min) to complement resistance work without causing excessive cortisol elevation.
- Protein and carb timing close to training help glucose disposal and recovery.

Testing and outcome measures
- Baseline and 12‑week measures: body weight, circumference (waist, hip), strength markers (e.g., 3–5RM on squat/bank/row), body composition if possible (DEXA or calipers), and repeat bloodwork (HbA1c per endocrinologist).
- Track session adherence, subjective energy and sleep weekly.

Sample microprogression example
- Bench 4×6 at 50 kg week 1 — add 1.25–2.5 kg when week 2–3 you can do 4×8 with good form. If stuck 2 weeks, reduce accessory volume and re‑test.
- If fatigue accumulates, swap a training day for mobility + technique and reduce finisher intensity.

Coach cues and practical coaching tips
- Emphasize full‑body tension in compound lifts, bracing, hip hinge for RDLs, knee tracking for squats.
- Keep tempo control on eccentric (2–3s) on accessory sets to increase time under tension without maximal load stress.
- Encourage consistent protein at each meal and include vegetables/fiber to slow glucose absorption.

Safety and follow up
- Continue communication with endocrinologist; check any med changes, glucose monitoring, and lab schedule.
- If client starts medication changes or develops symptoms (syncope, palpitations, severe fatigue), stop heavy training and refer for medical review.

If you want I can:
- Convert this into printable 12‑week weekly sheets with loads and progression templates.
- Provide specific sample menus for a moderate deficit and carb distribution tailored to target calorie and macro ranges.
- Create a tracking sheet for RPE, weight, sleep and cycle/energy.

Would you like printable weekly templates and a 7‑day sample meal plan matched to calorie/macros (include target kcal)?
